title: Finite tensor products of field extensions are nontrivial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $S$ be a finite set. For every $s\in S$ let $L_s/k$ be a field extension with structural embedding $a_s:k\to L_s$. Then the finite tensor product $\bigotimes_{s\in S,k}L_s$, equivalently the coproduct of the $L_s$ in commutative $k$-algebras, is nontrivial. For $S=\varnothing$ this coproduct is $k$.

source.place: Tag 0CNJ, lines 145-166: finite tensor products occur in the displayed filtered-colimit construction; the finite nontriviality statement is supplied as an auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Proceed by induction on the cardinality of the finite set $S$. If $S=\varnothing$, the coproduct is the base field $k$ by the empty-tensor convention in the statement, and it is nontrivial because a field has distinct zero and one.

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 0CNI (lemma-infinite-product), limits.tex lines 145-157, for finite tensor stages; the empty coproduct over k is k by the convention in the statement, and its nontriviality is elementary.

proof.text: For the induction step choose $s\in S$ and put $T=S\setminus\{s\}$. By induction the finite tensor coproduct $A_T=\bigotimes_{t\in T,k}L_t$ is nontrivial. Both $A_T$ and $L_s$ are nonzero vector spaces over the field $k$: $A_T$ has its scalar action through its coproduct structure map, and $L_s$ is a field extension. Therefore [lem-pur-field-vector-space-tensor-nontrivial] gives that $A_T\otimes_kL_s$ is nontrivial. The canonical associativity/rebracketing identification of a finite coproduct, obtained by applying the binary tensor pushout universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to the two subfamilies $T$ and $\{s\}$, identifies $A_T\otimes_kL_s$ with $\bigotimes_{u\in S,k}L_u$. Transporting nontriviality across this ring isomorphism proves the induction step, including the singleton case $T=\varnothing$.
